items.title: Investing.com’s stocks of the week
items.summary: Investing.com -- Democratic wins in both chambers of Congress eventually triggered a heavy sell-off across AI and chip names, while deal news drove sharp moves in both directions elsewhere.

items.title: Applied Materials Stocks Rise 4.7% as Chip Equipment Rallies Ahead of Earnings
items.summary: Applied Materials reports fiscal fourth-quarter results on November 12, after Lam Research's $25 billion buyback lifted the group.

items.title: Tesla Rebounds 5% as Musk Ends Cybertruck to Make Room for “Increased Cybercab Production”
items.summary: [IMAGE CREDIT: NASA/Aubrey Gemignani and SUMALI IBNU CHAMID from Alemedia. id via Canva] Key TakeawaysTesla rose 5% today after Elon Musk said it will wind down Cybertruck production in Texas around mid-2027 to build more Cybercabs.

items.title: Lam Research Soars 9% on $25 Billion Buyback as Chip Stocks Rebound From Rout
items.summary: Key TakeawaysLam Research shares jumped 9% today after its board approved a $25 billion buyback, outpacing ASML and the other chip-equipment makers in the rebound. Lam had no other news, so the buyback is the clearest reason for the extra gain, and it’s a strong vote of confidence.

items.title: Micron Soars 6% as Memory Stocks Bounce Back From Thursday’s 17% Crash
items.summary: Key TakeawaysMicron shares jumped 6% after IREN’s results eased fears that AI data-center spending is slowing. Seagate, Applied Materials and Nvidia ride the same AI build-out.

items.title: Premarket movers: Airbnb, Cloudflare, IREN rally; Atlassian, Five9 tumble
items.summary: Investing.com - U.S. stock futures pointed to a mixed open on Friday as chip stocks rebounded following a broad-based selloff in the previous session, offering some relief to investors worried about the impact of the Democratic midterm election victory on the artificial intelligence boom.
